questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that a stated assumption and a silent guess carry different risk, even when they're literally the same guess?
options: Because stated assumptions are always statistically more accurate than silent guesses
Because panels are not allowed to question stated assumptions
Because a silent guess that turns out wrong looks like a mistake, while the same guess stated openly looks like a documented, reasonable judgment call
Because silent guesses are against Salesforce's official certification rules
questions.explain: The content of the guess doesn't change — only whether the panel can see it was a deliberate, documented choice versus discovering an unstated gap on their own.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a risk-appetite assumption, per this lesson's categories?
options: Assuming peak order volume stays under a specific number per hour
Assuming the client has a budget for a Shield Platform Encryption add-on
Assuming a dealer network already has some identity provider in place
Assuming Alder Trust Bank would rather accept a slower onboarding flow than relax its two-approver segregation-of-duties rule
questions.explain: This is a judgment about how a client is likely to prioritize a trade-off based on their described context (a bank's regulatory posture), which is exactly what a risk-appetite assumption fills in.

questions.q: What distinguishes a strong assumptions section from a weak, defensive one, according to this lesson?
options: A strong one is short, specific, and states the concrete consequence if the assumption turns out to be wrong
A strong one lists every possible gap in the scenario, no matter how minor
A strong one avoids naming any numbers at all, to stay flexible
A strong one is written only after the panel asks a question about it
questions.explain: Naming the specific consequence of being wrong is what separates a real, evaluable assumption from a vague, excuse-like sentence that sounds thorough but commits to nothing.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say that writing an assumption down "invites" scrutiny rather than avoiding it?
options: Because stating an assumption guarantees the panel will never ask about it
Because a panelist questioning a stated assumption is giving the candidate a chance to show they already considered the consequence, unlike discovering the same unstated gap cold
Because panels are required to skip any topic a candidate already wrote down
Because stated assumptions legally bind the panel to accept the design
questions.explain: The same question lands very differently depending on whether it follows a stated assumption (showing foresight) or an undocumented gap (showing it was never considered).

questions.q: Why does Carrow Equipment's dealer-network scenario (Lesson 4) need an existing-technology-investment assumption about identity providers?
options: Because the scenario explicitly names every one of the 1,200 dealers' identity systems
Because identity providers are irrelevant to that scenario entirely
Because Salesforce requires every partner org to use the exact same identity provider
Because the scenario mentions some dealers running their own identity systems without specifying all dealers' setups, leaving a gap a design has to fill in with a stated assumption
questions.explain: The scenario leaves this detail open for most dealers, so a defensible design states an assumption about what's typically in place rather than silently guessing or ignoring the gap.
